headline: Southborough officials weighed a $38 million Neary School renovation and prepared for a potential multi-million-dollar operating override as FY28 budget planning began.
synopsis: Planning for the Margaret A. Neary Elementary School shifted significantly after architects determined that a baseline $15 million repair would yield under $6 million in direct construction, directing officials toward a $38 million addition-renovation plan. At the same time, municipal boards began grappling with a projected structural deficit exceeding $2 million for fiscal year 2028, requiring departments to model drastic reductions in case a Proposition 2 1/2 operational override fails. Ahead of the Special Town Meeting, committees finalized recommendations on landfill water extensions, debt rescissions, and Community Preservation Act funding for trails and golf course irrigation. The Planning Board pushed its Costco hearings into November while approving minor site plan modifications along Route 9. Meanwhile, the School Committee voted to align local teacher salary schedules with the regional high school starting in 2027.

top_items.title: Building Committee Shifts Toward $38M Neary Renovation Plan
top_items.why: A $15 million baseline upgrade would yield only $5.8 million in direct construction due to code mandates, prompting the building committee to advance a $38 million addition-renovation project.
top_items.body: Tappé Architects informed the Elementary School Building Committee that mandated fire sprinklers, accessibility upgrades, and soft costs would consume most of a $15 million baseline repair budget, leaving boiler replacements and classroom improvements unfunded. Committee members agreed to move forward with schematic design work for a comprehensive $38 million addition and renovation option. Separately, the ongoing Neary roof replacement was reported nearly 90 percent complete, with school officials projecting nearly $2 million in borrowed funds will be returned to the town.

top_items.title: Town Departments Model Reductions Amid Looming FY28 Deficit
top_items.why: Facing a projected structural deficit exceeding $2 million, municipal departments prepared level-funded budget scenarios detailing severe service cuts if an operating override fails.
top_items.body: Southborough town departments submitted preliminary fiscal year 2028 budget proposals under instructions to prepare both level-service requests and reduced level-funded plans. The Board of Health approved options warning that a failed override would necessitate closing offices on Fridays and delaying septic reviews. The Select Board and Advisory Committee scheduled joint sessions to evaluate departmental requests and discuss whether to seek a multi-year Proposition 2 1/2 operating override.

top_items.title: Capital Committee Reviews $2.15M Appropriations and $49M Borrowing
top_items.why: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee began vetting capital requests for FY28, including $2.15 million in appropriations and up to $49 million in bondable projects.
top_items.body: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee compiled initial department capital requests, which are dominated by school renovation proposals. Initial requests include $710,000 for local Southborough school maintenance, alongside substantial public works fleet replacements, police cruiser and camera leasing, and fire equipment. The committee requested detailed inventory plans, written memos, and in-person presentations from department heads to prioritize projects ahead of a joint presentation in December.

top_items.title: Boards Finalize Positions for October Special Town Meeting
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee recommended $240,000 to extend town water near the Parkerville landfill, while town boards locked in stances on fall warrant articles.
top_items.body: The Advisory Committee unanimously endorsed Article 7 after confirming the town will fund the entire cost to connect two homes near the capped Parkerville Road landfill to town water. Meanwhile, the Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to keep the full $217,318 funding request for the Peninsula Trail footbridge on the warrant despite opposition from the Select Board and Advisory Committee. The Select Board also voted unanimously against retaining $100,000 in unissued borrowing authority for Breakneck Hill restoration, supporting full debt rescission.

top_items.title: Planning Board Extends Costco Review and Approves Route 9 Sites
top_items.why: The Planning Board extended its decision deadline for the proposed Costco to December 18, 2026, while approving site plan modifications for two other commercial properties.
top_items.body: The Planning Board scheduled a special meeting on November 2, 2026, and extended its statutory decision deadline to December 18 for the major site plan and special permits for the 167,000-square-foot Costco at 21 Coslin Drive while awaiting peer reviews. At the same meeting, the board voted 4-0 to approve major site plan modifications for the golf driving range at 22 Turnpike Road and the Chase Bank branch at 154 Turnpike Road, attaching conditions on site lighting, landscaping, and stormwater controls.

top_items.title: Regional School Subcommittees Identify Debt Drop and Health Savings
top_items.why: Regional school officials identified an upcoming $800,000 net decrease in high school debt service and up to $600,000 in potential health insurance savings for FY28.
top_items.body: Subcommittees of the Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee reviewed the FY28 budget outlook, noting that the expiration of 2004 high school building debt will produce an estimated $800,000 net drop in regional debt service even with new borrowing for the athletic complex. District leaders also outlined efforts to restructure employee health insurance deductibles to mirror state plans, which could yield roughly $600,000 in regional operating savings. Capital requests for Algonquin Regional High School were clarified to include five projects totaling approximately $460,000.

top_items.title: School Committee Aligns Teacher Pay Scale with Regional High School
top_items.why: The Southborough School Committee voted 5-0 to amend the teachers contract, adjusting retirement incentives and linking salary scales to Algonquin starting July 2027.
top_items.body: Following executive session, the Southborough School Committee voted unanimously to approve amendments to the collective bargaining agreement with the Southborough Teachers Association Unit A. The amendments revise the district retirement incentive program and align Southborough teacher salary schedules with the Algonquin Regional High School agreement effective July 1, 2027. In the current year, administrators reported that the FY27 operating budget remains stable with a $349,347 available balance after absorbing two elementary teacher hires.
